leads.title: Custom server trust handling
leads.attacker_control: Network endpoint and certificate presented to the app
leads.possible_impact: Acceptance of an untrusted server identity
leads.next_test: In an authorized test environment, verify whether an invalid server certificate is rejected.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Use platform trust evaluation and reject untrusted certificates.
leads.attack_scenario: If the app accepts an invalid server identity, someone able to present that identity on its network path could impersonate the service. An API reference alone does not show that trust is bypassed.

leads.title: External URL handler
leads.attacker_control: Parameters supplied through another app or browser
leads.possible_impact: Unauthorized app action or access to protected content
leads.next_test: Open a controlled link while signed out and under a second test account; compare authorized and unauthorized outcomes.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Validate every parameter and enforce authorization in the handler.
leads.attack_scenario: If an external link parameter reaches a protected app action without authorization, a sender could use a crafted link to invoke that action. An API-name reference does not establish a reachable handler.

leads.title: Check whether the declared URL scheme permits a protected action after sign-out
leads.attacker_control: A benign link and its parameters, opened on a test device
leads.possible_impact: A protected action could occur without the expected account authorization if the handler fails to recheck it
leads.next_test: Under a test account, record the authorized result; sign out and repeat the same benign link; then try a second test account with an object belonging to the first
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Determine the root cause after reproducing the behavior.
leads.priority_reason: The scheme is a documented external entry point that can receive controlled parameters
leads.disconfirming_result: The app rejects the action when signed out and under the second account
leads.missing_evidence: Handler behavior, authorization checks, and repeatable test results
leads.attack_scenario: If the link handler uses those parameters for a protected action without checking the current account, a link sender could cause that action when the recipient opens it. Handler behavior is unverified.

leads.title: Custom server trust handling needs review
leads.attacker_control: A network endpoint or certificate presented to the app in an authorized test setup
leads.possible_impact: The app could accept an untrusted server identity if the custom path bypasses validation
leads.next_test: Trace the trust callback, then check whether the assessed build rejects an invalid certificate in a controlled environment.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Review the full trust validation path; do not accept a server certificate without proper validation.
leads.disconfirming_result: The invalid certificate is rejected and platform trust validation remains required.
leads.attack_scenario: If the custom trust callback accepts an invalid server identity, someone able to present that identity on the app's network path could impersonate the service and observe or alter traffic. Acceptance is unverified.

leads.title: Test custom url scheme: exampleapp
leads.possible_impact: Unauthorized app action or protected-content access
leads.next_test: Open a controlled link while signed out and as a second test account; check authorization and input handling.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Validate link input and enforce authorization for every requested action.
leads.attack_scenario: If the app acts on parameters from a custom link without checking the current account, a sender could use a link to request an unauthorized action. The handler behavior is untested.

leads.title: Test document type: public.json
leads.attacker_control: A document opened by the user
leads.possible_impact: Unexpected file access, parser failure, or unintended app action
leads.next_test: Open a benign test document of this type and inspect import validation and file access.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Validate document structure and restrict imports to required types and access.
leads.attack_scenario: If the app imports a file supplied by another party and its parser mishandles that content, opening the file could trigger unintended behavior. No parser flaw is established by the declaration.

leads.title: Trace external links into web code
leads.attacker_control: A controlled link and its parameters
leads.possible_impact: Script execution or content injection if link data reaches a web sink
leads.next_test: Trace the link handler to the bundled web code, then pass a benign marker through a controlled link and observe whether it reaches the sink.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: If a path is confirmed, validate link data and replace unsafe dynamic code or HTML writes.
leads.disconfirming_result: The handler does not pass link-controlled data to the sink, or the data is safely handled before rendering or execution.
leads.attack_scenario: If a link parameter flows into the bundled dynamic-code or HTML-writing call, a link sender could influence WebView content. The two clues coexist, but no data flow has been traced.

path_analysis.missing_link: No path from a link parameter to the bundled web-code sink has been verified.

leads.title: Dynamic JavaScript execution needs input review
leads.attacker_control: JavaScript input, if a link, message, or network response reaches the call
leads.possible_impact: Untrusted input could execute script with the WebView's privileges
leads.next_test: Trace the call's argument to its sources; use a benign marker from a controlled source to check whether input reaches execution.
leads.remediation_if_confirmed: Avoid executing constructed code. If input can come from a link, message, or network response, validate the path and replace dynamic execution.
leads.disconfirming_result: The argument is a fixed trusted string, or controlled untrusted input never reaches the call.
leads.attack_scenario: If a link, message, or response controls the string passed to dynamic JavaScript execution, its sender could run script in that WebView context. No input-to-sink path has been shown.
